title: Generated-regressor Monte Carlo for the break-demeaned ELW d-hat

design.arm_a: simulate -> Bai-Perron re-estimates breaks -> demean -> ELW (realistic)
design.arm_b: simulate -> demean at TRUE simulated breaks -> ELW (oracle)
design.dgp: ARFIMA(0, d_hat, 0) Gaussian innovations + the fitted piecewise-constant level implanted at the estimated break dates
design.arm_b_scope_correction_rev3: Arm B oracle-ises the break PARTITION (count plus locations). It still calls piecewise_demean on the simulated series, i.e. it re-estimates each segment mean, so it is NOT an 'ELW alone' baseline. See claim_corrections_rev3.arm_b_is_not_pure_elw_only.

summary.finding_1_se_is_understated: The published asymptotic SE understates the Monte Carlo sampling sd by a factor of 1.21-1.33. The original confidence intervals are too narrow.
summary.finding_2_but_not_mainly_because_of_the_: Contrary to what the reviewer critique might suggest, break ESTIMATION contributes only 1.01-1.10x on top of the oracle-break sd -- i.e. the generated-regressor effect on the SE is SMALL. Most of the understatement comes from the asymptotic 1/(2 sqrt(m)) formula itself being optimistic at this sample size and bandwidth. Reported this way round because it is what the simulation shows, not what would best support the critique.
summary.finding_3_downward_attenuation: Re-estimating breaks and demeaning attenuates d-hat downward by -0.085 to -0.027 even when the simulated DGP contains EXACTLY the level shifts being removed and no others. So part of the raw -> demeaned d-hat drop reported in the original round is a mechanical artefact of fitting breaks, not evidence of additional level shifts. This weakens the original round's reading of that drop in BOTH directions and is a further reason the identification claim does not stand.
summary.finding_4_break_recovery_is_noisy: Bai-Perron recovers the exact number of breaks in 7%-78% of replications (TW0050 worst at 7%). Break DATES are estimated with substantial uncertainty even where the resulting d-hat sd is not much inflated.
summary.what_survives: The descriptive statement survives comfortably: with MC sd of 0.045-0.063 and d-hat of 0.457-0.645, the ratio d/sd is 7.4-12.5, so the break-demeaned d-hat is still clearly positive under this model. That is a statement about RESIDUAL PERSISTENCE, not an identification result -- the retracted claim stays retracted, because no amount of SE correction can make a deterministic 5-break model speak to a random dense-shift alternative.
summary.READ_THIS_FIRST_rev3_supersessions: TWO ENTRIES IN THIS `summary` BLOCK ARE SUPERSEDED -- see claim_corrections_rev3 for the full record. (1) finding_3_downward_attenuation attributes the whole -0.085..-0.027 arm-A bias to break estimation. It does not: the correct, paired A-minus-B figure is -0.056 to -0.020, roughly half. (2) finding_4_break_recovery_is_noisy ends with a claim about break DATE uncertainty. RETRACTED: this simulation stores only break COUNTS and never compares dates. The original strings are retained verbatim, not rewritten, so that the record of what was claimed survives alongside the correction.

scope_limits: MODEL-CONDITIONAL: assumes the DGP really is ARFIMA + deterministic breaks at the estimated dates. It quantifies sampling uncertainty under that model.
It is NOT a test of that model and NOT evidence for it.
It cannot address Diebold-Inoue (random / dense shift DGP), which is the identification question this experiment RETRACTS rather than answers.
Gaussian innovations; log-RV is closer to Gaussian than RV but not exactly so.
The same FD_MAXK = 2000 truncation binds here as in the main round.

ARM B IS NOT ELW-ONLY (added rev3): the oracle arm knows the break DATES but still estimates the segment MEANS from simulated data. The A-minus-B contrast therefore isolates the cost of selecting the break partition and differences out the mean-estimation generated-regressor uncertainty, which this design does not measure.

claim_corrections_rev3.status: This frozen artifact predates the corrections listed here. Its original fields are retained verbatim for audit; the entries below say which of its CLAIMS no longer hold and what replaces them. Where a corrected number is given it was computed from fields already present in this same file (arm means and d_demeaned_fitted), not from a re-run.
claim_corrections_rev3.raised_by: Codex gpt-5.6-sol round 2 review of K1623 rev2, section 7 (BLOCKER)
claim_corrections_rev3.applied_at_round: rev3 (claim-alignment only; no estimation was re-run)
claim_corrections_rev3.source_of_truth: k1623_rev2_mc.py as it now stands already emits the corrected fields (break_partition_selection_attenuation_a_minus_b, arm_b_oracle_partition_bias). This artifact was generated by the earlier draft and is NOT regenerated in rev3, which is exactly why the discrepancy has to be annotated here rather than hidden.

superseded_claims.superseded_text: Re-estimating breaks and demeaning attenuates d-hat downward by -0.085 to -0.027 ...
superseded_claims.why_it_is_wrong: That range is arm A's TOTAL bias against the fitted d-hat. It is the sum of (i) the bias the oracle-break arm B already shows and (ii) the extra attenuation from BIC having to select the break partition (both count and locations). Attributing the total to break estimation overstates that effect roughly two-fold.
superseded_claims.corrected_claim: The part attributable to BIC selecting the break partition (count plus locations) is the paired A-minus-B contrast: -0.056 to -0.020. Arm B is itself biased by -0.039 to -0.007 (ELW finite-sample behaviour PLUS estimating the segment means at known locations -- see arm_b_is_not_pure_elw_only). The qualitative point is unchanged: part of the original round's raw -> demeaned d-hat drop is a mechanical artefact of fitting breaks.

superseded_claims.why_it_is_wrong: Retained unchanged and still numerically correct AS arm A's total bias, but its NAME invites reading it as the attenuation caused by break estimation, which it is not.
superseded_claims.corrected_claim: Use break_partition_selection_effect_range_a_minus_b below for the break-estimation effect. Read this field only as 'total arm-A bias vs the fitted d-hat'.

superseded_claims.superseded_text: Break DATES are estimated with substantial uncertainty even where the resulting d-hat sd is not much inflated.
superseded_claims.why_it_is_wrong: RETRACTED as unsupported by this artifact. The simulation stores only the selected break COUNT; it never stores or compares estimated break DATES, so it cannot quantify date-location error in either direction. k1623_rev2_mc.py already concedes this in its own finding_4 text.
superseded_claims.corrected_claim: Only the COUNT recovery rate is supported: Bai-Perron recovers the exact number of breaks in 7%-78% of replications (TW0050 worst at 7%). No statement about break-date uncertainty is made.

superseded_claims.superseded_text: arm B = oracle; 'Arm B isolates the sampling noise of ELW alone'.
superseded_claims.why_it_is_wrong: Arm B calls piecewise_demean on the SIMULATED data, so it estimates each segment's mean from that data. It oracle-ises the entire break PARTITION (count plus locations); it does not use the known implanted levels. So it is not an ELW-only baseline, and the mean-structure generated-regressor uncertainty it still carries is DIFFERENCED OUT of the A-minus-B contrast.
superseded_claims.corrected_claim: sd(A)/sd(B) = 1.01-1.10x and the A-minus-B bias contrast both measure the cost of selecting the break partition (count plus locations), conditional on the segment means being re-estimated in both arms. The total generated-regressor burden of the estimated mean structure is therefore NOT bounded by these figures -- it is not measured by this design at all.

corrected_attribution.definition: total_arm_a_bias = arm_a.mean - d_demeaned_fitted; arm_b_oracle_partition_bias = arm_b.mean - d_demeaned_fitted; break_partition_selection_effect = arm_a.mean - arm_b.mean.

arm_b_is_not_pure_elw_only.what_arm_b_actually_does: k1623_rev2_mc.py:118-120 -- K.piecewise_demean(x, breaks_true): the break PARTITION (count and locations) is the true simulated one, but each segment's mean is estimated from the simulated series.
arm_b_is_not_pure_elw_only.consequence: Arm B is an oracle in the break PARTITION (count plus locations). It is NOT 'ELW alone' and NOT free of generated-regressor uncertainty: it still estimates k+1 segment means. Any contrast against arm B therefore isolates the partition-selection cost and is SILENT about the mean-estimation cost.
arm_b_is_not_pure_elw_only.what_would_measure_the_rest: A third arm that demeans with the KNOWN implanted level vector instead of re-estimating segment means. That arm does not exist in this design and rev3 does not add it (no-recompute scope).
